newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks close sharply lower.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks close sharply lower.

text.p: Australian shares closed sharply lower on Friday as profit-taking erased all of Thursday's record-breaking gains following another fall on Wall Street.
Options exercises, following Thursday's October series expiries, drove volumes and the vast majority of turnover put through the market was before the start of trade.
The benchmark All Ordinaries index ended 42.4 points lower at 2,335.2, it biggest one day fall since July 16.

Stuart Smith, senior dealer at Brisbane brokerage Lance Jones, said he believed the sharpness of the fall reflected the market's disappointment that the Reserve Bank did not move to lower rates on Friday morning.
"Basically there was too much euphoric buying yesterday on comments from the prime minister that the wages data would prompt a rate cut," Stuart said.

Dealers said falls were across the board although blue chip issues bore the brunt of selling activity especially the big resource issues CRA, WMC and BHP following their steady rises earlier this week.

One of the few bright areas for the market was the wine sector with a number of the small capitalised wineries forging ahead after Brian McGuigan Wines reported strong first quarter earnings on Thursday.
